_note: Waivers for the unslop crafted-floor gate. Each is a claim about why the check misreads this repo, not permission to ignore it. substance.legal is deliberately NOT waived — it is a real gap and it needs a human.

waivers.reason: Every finding of this rule is inside web/out/, the gitignored Next export, not source. The detector runs as its own subprocess and does not share unslop's SKIP_TOP_LEVEL_DIRS, so it walks the build output the survey correctly skips. Verified by running detect.mjs directly against web/app, web/components and web/remotion: 0 findings in all three.

The typeface decision is real and documented, it is simply not a literal font-family with a face name. globals.css declares --sans (system grotesk stack) and --mono, and every rule consumes font-family: var(--sans|--mono). The decision, including why no webfont is loaded, is stated in DESIGN.md under Typeface.

Authored voice, kept deliberately. Em dashes are this repo's house punctuation across commits, docs and product copy, and they are load-bearing in a voice that qualifies its own claims mid-sentence. DESIGN.md states this under Voice. Stripping 112 of them would remove the author's register to move a counter, which is precisely what the voice doctrine forbids.

The two remaining sites are a check mark used as notation inside a mono technical readout in a Remotion film frame (AcceptGate), where it marks a satisfied condition in a terminal-style status column. It is data notation, not decoration. The one real UI control that was a typed glyph, the play/pause button, is now drawn as SVG instead.
Same two AcceptGate sites as copy.emoji: a status column inside a rendered composition, not a marketing bullet list. There is no checkmark-bulleted feature list anywhere in this product's copy.

Real product evidence exists and is shipped: web/public/cinema carries five Veo-generated MP4 clips and six WebP posters, all of which render on /demo, plus docs/backup-demo.mp4 driven against the live hub. The gate looks for public/screenshots or public/media by name, so it misses a directory called cinema. This is a naming-convention miss, not an absence.

Reported SKIP as no motion detected, which is wrong: this site is largely motion. prefers-reduced-motion is honoured in DemoCinema, AsciiField, MotionPanel, Cinema and AutoScroll, and in every case the reduced path lands on the finished figure rather than a degraded one. Recorded here so the SKIP is not mistaken for an unexamined surface.
